status.title: Status
status.backupBody: The database and uploaded files are backed up automatically, and the most recent backups are kept. After an incident, an administrator restores the latest backup with a single command; changes made after that backup are lost.

about.title: About this demo
about.intro: Task Manager is a collaborative project and task manager, built at 42 by Eraad, khderdou, ksupinsk and nratajcz for the ft_transcendence project. This copy is a local demo: explore it freely.

features.projects: Create projects and invite members as Owner, Editor or Viewer.
features.tasks: Follow tasks by status, with a description, attached files and a banner image.
features.discussion: Comment on tasks and talk with your team on each project's message wall.
features.search: Search tasks and projects with filters, sorting and pages.
features.gamification: Unlock achievements, earn XP, level up and collect badges.
features.api: Connect other tools through the public API with a personal API key.
features.privacy: Download a copy of your data or delete your account at any time.
features.languages: Use the app in English, French or Spanish.

about.stackBody: A React 19 interface (Vite, Tailwind CSS) talks to a FastAPI backend (Python, SQLAlchemy) backed by PostgreSQL 17. nginx serves everything over HTTPS, and the whole stack runs in Docker Compose with automatic backups.

limits.local: It runs only on this computer (https://localhost); it is not an online service.
limits.certificate: The HTTPS certificate is self-signed, so your browser shows a warning the first time.
limits.google: “Continue with Google” works only if this copy has been given its own Google credentials.
limits.email: Emails (data download and account deletion confirmations) land in a local test inbox and are never delivered.
limits.refresh: Project pages refresh every 15 seconds, so other members' changes are not instant.
limits.api: API keys are managed through the API documentation (/docs), without a screen of their own.
limits.reset: Demo data can be reset at any time: do not store anything important.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy

collect.title: 1. Data we collect
collect.body: When you create an account, we collect your username, email address and password. If you sign in with Google, we receive your Google account ID, email address and profile picture instead of a password. We also store what you create in Task Manager: projects, tasks, comments, messages, files and API keys, plus your progress (XP, achievements and badges). Your browser keeps your sign-in token and your language choice in its local storage. Signing in with Google also sets a cookie that lasts 10 minutes and only protects that sign-in. We use no advertising or tracking cookies.

use.title: 2. How we use your data
use.body: We use your data only to run Task Manager: signing you in, managing your projects and sending emails about your account. We never use it for advertising or profiling.

sharing.title: 3. Sharing your data
sharing.body: We do not sell your data or share it with third parties. Project content is visible to the project's members, and service administrators can access your account to keep the service running.

security.title: 4. Security
security.body: We protect your data with appropriate measures: encrypted connections, passwords never stored in plain text, and restricted access.

retention.title: 5. Data retention
retention.body: We keep your data for as long as your account exists. Automatic backups keep the latest copies of the database and files (by default one per hour, for 24 hours), so deleted data can remain in them for about a day.

rights.title: 6. Your rights
rights.intro: Under the GDPR, you can at any time:

items.access: access and download your data from your Profile page;
items.rectification: correct your username from your Profile page (contact an administrator to change your email);
items.erasure: delete your account from your Profile page;
items.objection: object to or restrict the use of your data by contacting an administrator.

rights.footer: Each download or deletion is confirmed by email.

deletion.title: 7. Deleting your account
deletion.body: You can delete your account at any time from your Profile page. Your personal data is then permanently erased. Projects, tasks and files shared with other members stay available to them, without your name.

privacy.contactBody: For any question about your data, contact the Task Manager team.

purpose.title: 1. Purpose
purpose.body: Task Manager is a collaborative project and task manager built by students at 42 for the ft_transcendence project. This copy is a demo that runs on your own computer. By creating an account, you accept these terms.

account.title: 2. Your account
account.body: You are responsible for keeping the information used to sign in to your account confidential, and for all activity carried out from it. Provide accurate information when you create it. You can delete your account at any time from your Profile page.

use.title: 3. Acceptable use
use.body: Use the platform lawfully: do not store or share illegal, hateful or harmful content. Do not try to access projects you are not a member of, to break the platform's security or to overload it; sign-in and public API requests are rate limited.

content.title: 4. Your content
content.body: What you create (projects, tasks, comments, messages and files) stays yours. Every member of a project can see its content; the project owner decides who joins and with which role (Owner, Editor or Viewer). Files must use an allowed format and stay within the size limit.

api.title: 5. Public API and API keys
api.body: An API key gives access to your data through the public API. Keep it as secret as a password and revoke any key you think has leaked. Excessive use can be limited.

moderation.title: 6. Moderation
moderation.body: Administrators can ban or delete an account that breaks these terms. A banned account can no longer sign in or use its API keys.

liability.title: 7. Availability and liability
liability.body: Task Manager is a student project provided as is, with no guarantee of availability. Data may be reset at any time: keep your own copy (Profile → My data → Download my data). Automatic backups exist, but they are not a promise of recovery.

changes.title: 8. Changes to these terms
changes.body: These terms may change. The date at the top shows the latest version; using Task Manager after a change means you accept it.

rules.xp: You earn XP by unlocking achievements. Each achievement unlocks once per account.
rules.levels: Your level depends on your total XP and goes up to level 100.
rules.badges: Badges are earned at levels 5, 10, 25, 50 and 100. Your highest badge becomes your title, shown next to your name.
rules.counts: Progress counts what you do in the app. Each project, task, comment, file, message or teammate counts once, forever.
